generation.forced_text:
I never imagined how much one tiny, seemingly innocuos stone on the old path through town Square had changed so profoundly. It’s an ordinary place - my favorite part of a quiet, quaint small American city that I grew to know as my own as a teenager. The path was a main walk that led down a few steps, to where an archeology museum had long ago stood, now gone, its place filled instead a grass and wildflowers in this corner. It used be lined, as I remember in 90's - with stone and bricks and moss.

That's not all. I'd been there many times as my friends, parents even, took in this quiet, lovely space, but one day as I meaded along the stone, a detail struck a cord and brought back memories and feelings, that until today still linger with clarity
